<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Human rights violations during the Syrian Civil War]]
***[[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] releases an execution video showing a prisoner being killed by explosives in [[Yarmouk Camp]], [[Damascus]]. [http://metro.co.uk/2018/05/01/isis-prisoner-turned-human-bomb-latest-depraved-execution-video-7512459/ (''Metro'')]
**At least 23 civilians die in an airstrike near Shadadi, [[Al-Hasakah Governorate]]. The [[Syrian Observatory for Human Rights]] has stated it is not clear who carried out the attack, listing [[Iraq]] and [[American-led intervention in the Syrian Civil War|US-led coalition]] as two possibilities. The state-run [[Syrian Arab News Agency]] claims the US-led coalition is responsible. [http://home.bt.com/news/world-news/airstrikes-in-islamic-state-held-part-of-syria-kill-23-11364267968652 (BT)] [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20180502-23-civilians-killed-in-syria-in-suspected-us-coalition-air-strikes/ (Middle East Monitor)]
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**A suicide bombing kills at least 24 people at a mosque in [[Mubi (town)|Mubi]], [[Nigeria]]. [[Boko Haram]] are suspected of being behind the attack. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-43967738 (BBC)]
*[[Yemeni Crisis (2011–present)]]
**Pro-[[Abdrabbuh Mansur Hadi|Hadi]] forces capture the Al Bareh Triangle and seize [[Houthi]] arms. [https://gulfnews.com/news/gulf/yemen/yemen-army-retrieves-abandoned-al-houthi-arms-1.2214709 (''Gulf News'')]
**Several independent MPs urge [[Sudan]]ese [[president of Sudan|President]] [[Omar Al-Bashir]] to withdraw troops from [[Yemen]] where they are supporting a [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]]-led coalition fighting [[Houthi]] rebels. [http://allafrica.com/stories/201805010338.html (AllAfrica)]
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**[[Palestinian Islamic Jihad]] releases video of [[Israel]]i general [[Yoav Mordechai]] meeting with United Kingdom ambassador [[David Quarrey]] and observing the protests last week. Quarrey's visit came amid concerns of the [[Israeli Defence Forces]] using live ammunition and was intended to be kept secret. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2018/05/01/british-ambassador-israel-filmed-islamic-terrorist-group-secret/ (''The Telegraph'')]
*[[Persecution of Muslims in Myanmar]]
**[[Myanmar]]'s [[Tatmadaw|military]] pledges to a [[United Nations|U.N.]] delegation visiting [[Rakhine State]] that they will take "harsh" action against perpetrators of sexual violence in the region. The U.N. previously accused Myanmar's military of committing an [[ethnic cleansing]] of [[Rohingya people|Rohingya Muslims]] in Rakhine State. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-rohingya-un/myanmar-military-assures-un-of-harsh-action-on-sexual-assault-idUSKBN1I22VL (Reuters)]
*[[Iraq]]i police and [[al-Hashd al-Shaabi]] troops raid [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] locations in [[Hawija]], [[Kirkuk]], and seize tunnels and arms caches. [https://www.iraqinews.com/iraq-war/iraqi-troops-raid-several-islamic-state-tunnels-hotbeds-in-oil-rich-kirkuk/ (Iraqi News)]
*A bomb in [[Mosul]], [[Iraq]], kills and injures seven policemen. [https://www.iraqinews.com/iraq-war/7-policemen-killed-injured-in-deadly-bomb-attack-at-iraqi-train-station/ (Iraqi News)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Harvey Weinstein sexual abuse allegations]]
**American actress [[Ashley Judd]] sues [[Harvey Weinstein]] for defamation and sexual harassment, claiming he "torpedoed" her chance to be cast in [[The Lord of the Rings (film series)|''The Lord of the Rings'' trilogy]]. [http://www.heraldcourier.com/community/entertainment/ashley-judd-sues-harvey-weinstein-for-defamation-and-sexual-harassment/article_2359d5f2-9b44-5417-9f01-990dd1dbcf9c.html (''Herald Courier'')]
*Publisher [[Bloomsbury Publishing|Bloomsbury]] acquires [[Middle East]] and political publishing specialist [[I.B. Tauris]]. [https://www.thebookseller.com/news/bloomsbury-acquires-ib-tauris-776556 (The Bookseller)]
*The [[Supreme Court of India|Supreme Court]] of [[India]] orders the government to seek international help after examining photos submitted by environmentalists showing a change in colour of the [[Taj Mahal]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-india-43967685 (BBC)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economy of the United Kingdom]]
**Following the cancellation of the [[Williams & Glyn]] bank formation, the [[Royal Bank of Scotland]] announces the closure of 162 RBS and subsidiary [[NatWest]] branches across the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-43964273 (BBC)]
**[[Alcohol (Minimum Pricing) (Scotland) Act 2012|Minimum alcohol pricing]] comes into effect in [[Scotland]], mandating prices of at least 50[[pound sterling|p]] per [[Unit of alcohol|unit]]. Scotland becomes the first country to introduce such a scheme. [https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/scotland-minimum-alcohol-prices-cost-50p-unit-frosty-jack-strongbow-smirnoff-vodka-cider-whisky-wine-a8330681.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[United States]] guitar manufacturer [[Gibson (guitar company)|Gibson]] files for bankruptcy protection. [https://www.theguardian.com/business/2018/may/01/gibson-guitar-firm-files-for-bankruptcy-protection (''The Guardian'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Incidents at Universal parks]]
**At [[Universal Studios Japan]], the [[The Flying Dinosaur|Flying Dinosaur]] [[roller coaster]] gets stuck 100 feet in the air, stranding about 64 people for nearly two hours. [https://www.ndtv.com/offbeat/japan-rollercoaster-gets-stuck-riders-left-hanging-upside-down-for-hours-1845639 (NDTV)]
*[[Edifício Wilton Paes de Almeida]], a 26-story tower block in [[São Paulo]], Brazil, is destroyed by a fire and consequent collapse. Neighbouring buildings are also damaged by fire. Authorities warn the casualty toll is "likely to be high". [http://metro.co.uk/2018/05/01/residential-tower-block-collapses-huge-fire-rips-building-7511628/ (''Metro'')]
*An [[avalanche]] in the [[Alps]] kills three skiers and injures two in [[Valais]], [[Switzerland]]. [https://gulfnews.com/news/europe/switzerland/swiss-alps-avalanche-leaves-3-dead-2-injured-near-glacier-1.2198008 (''Gulf News'')]

;International relations
*[[Dominican Republic–Taiwan relations]], [[China–Dominican Republic relations]]
**The [[Dominican Republic]] severs ties with [[Taiwan]] and establishes diplomatic relations with [[China]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2018/05/01/asia/china-taiwan-dominican-republican-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Russia–United States relations]]
**A [[Russia]]n [[Su-27]] [[fighter jet]] intercepts a [[United States]] [[Boeing P-8 Poseidon|P-8 Poseidon]] surveillance plane in international airspace over the [[Baltic Sea]], with the US claiming the procedure was unprofessional and the aircraft came within 20 feet of each other. [https://www.kfdi.com/news/national/russian-fighter-jet-intercepts-us-navy-plane (KFDI)]
*[[Iran–Morocco relations]]
**[[Morocco]] cuts diplomatic ties with [[Iran]] over its support for the [[Polisario Front]], a [[Western Sahara]]n independence movement. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/05/morocco-cuts-diplomatic-ties-iran-western-sahara-feud-180501173229190.html (Al Jazeera)]
*The [[Africa]]n Land Forces Summit opens in [[Abuja]], [[Nigeria]]. Present are military delegations from 30 African nations plus representatives from [[Europe]] and the [[United States]]. [http://allafrica.com/view/group/main/main/id/00060314.html (AllAfrica)]
*[[Poland]] takes over the rotating Presidency of the [[United Nations]] [[UN Security Council|Security Council]]. [http://thenews.pl/1/10/Artykul/361449,Poland-takes-over-UN-Security-Council-presidency (Radio Poland)]

;Law and crime
*[[Terrorism in England]]
**[[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] suspect Lewis Ludlow makes an initial appearance before [[Westminster Magistrates' Court]] accused of plotting a terror attack in [[London]]. He denies the offences and the case is transferred to the [[Old Bailey]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-kent-43962721 (BBC)]
*[[May Day]]
**[[Far-left]] anarchists clash with riot police in central [[Paris]], [[France]]. Several businesses are looted and set on fire, including a [[McDonald's]] restaurant and [[Renault]] garage. Hundreds are arrested. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-may-day-france/riot-police-use-teargas-against-anarchists-at-paris-may-day-rally-idUSKBN1I23TG (Reuters)]
*[[Far-right terrorism in the United Kingdom]]
**[[West Midlands Police]] arrest five men and a woman suspected of membership of [[National Action (UK)|National Action]], a [[neo-Nazi]] group banned as a terror group. [http://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/news/yourtown/banbury/15804237.Man_and_woman_arrested_over_membership_of_neo-Nazi_group__National_Action_/ (''The Oxford Mail'')]
*[[Iran]] bans the [[Telegram (software)|Telegram]] messenger app, citing national security concerns. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-43963927 (BBC)]
*[[Catherine De Bolle]] from [[Belgium]] becomes the first woman to lead [[Europol]]. [https://www.politico.eu/article/europol-europes-terror-defenses-pass-to-belgian-hands-eu-law-enforcement-agency-catherine-de-bolle/ (''Politico'')]
;Politics and elections
*[[2018 Iraqi parliamentary election]]
**[[Muntadhar al-Zaidi]], the Iraqi journalist [[George W. Bush shoe-throwing incident|who threw his shoes]] at [[George W. Bush]] in [[2008]], will run for [[Council of Representatives of Iraq|Iraqi parliament]]. [https://www.buzzfeed.com/hayesbrown/george-w-bush-shoe-throw-president-iraq (''BuzzFeed News'')]
*[[2017–18 United States political sexual scandals]]
**[[Louisiana Secretary of State]] [[Tom Schedler]] announces that he will resign in one week, after being accused of sexual harassment. [http://www.nola.com/politics/index.ssf/2018/04/tom_schedler_resigns_as_secret.html (''The Times-Picayune'')]

;Sports
*[[Kenya]]n boxer Brian Agina goes missing as his team prepares to return from the [[Commonwealth Games]] in [[Australia]]. [http://allafrica.com/view/group/main/main/id/00060302.html (AllAfrica)]
*Former [[Green Bay Packers]] and [[NC State Wolfpack football|NC State]] player Carlos Gray is found dead after being shot at his home. [http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/article210208509.html (''News Observer'')]
